title: Nyingma Gyubum (rnying ma rgyud 'bum, the Collected Tantras of the Ancients)
summary: The canon of Old Tantras not (or only partly) admitted to the Kangyur: the tantras of Atiyoga (mind, space and instruction series, incl. the Seventeen Tantras), Anuyoga (the root sūtras) and Mahāyoga (tantra section and sādhana section), with protector texts. Compiled in its extant form from the 15th c.

attribution.tradition: The tantras were taught by the buddhas of the three kāyas and translated in the first diffusion; Ratna Lingpa (1403-1479) gathered them into a collection.
attribution.scholarly: Several editions (Tingkye, Tsamdrag, Derge, Kathmandu) differ in contents and order; the Derge edition was prepared under Getse Paṇḍita in the late 18th c.

structure.description: Arranged by vehicle: Atiyoga, Anuyoga, Mahāyoga; editions of c. 25-46 volumes (exact counts differ by edition; not recorded here)

notes: Not local. Volume counts omitted deliberately (see REPORT.md).

title: Nyingma Kama (rnying ma bka' ma, the Canonical Transmission)
summary: The collection of the 'spoken word' lineage of the Nyingma: the three inner tantras with their commentaries, empowerment and sādhana texts transmitted without interruption from the first diffusion (as distinct from treasures). Edited at Mindroling by Terdak Lingpa and Lochen Dharmaśrī, and greatly expanded by Dudjom Rinpoche in the 20th c.

title: The Māyājāla (sgyu 'phrul drva ba) cycle of tantras
summary: The family of Mahāyoga tantras of the 'Magical Net' to which the Guhyagarbha belongs: in the Derge Old Tantra section the Guhyagarbha root (Tōh 832), the 'Mirror of All Secrets' (Tōh 833), a longer Guhyagarbha (Tōh 834), the 'Great Magical Net of the Goddess' (Tōh 836) and the 'Great Supreme Uttara' of the Guhyagarbha (Tōh 837). Tradition counts eight Māyājāla tantras (sgyu 'phrul sde brgyad).

notes: Existence and titles checked in the local catalogue (Derge-Kangyur D832-D837); the grouping of eight is from memory.

title: Guhyagarbha Tantra (dpal gsang ba'i snying po de kho na nyid rnam par nges pa)
summary: The root tantra of Mahāyoga in 22 chapters: in Akaniṣṭha the buddhas teach that all phenomena are primordially enlightened, that the aggregates and elements are the male and female buddhas, and set out bodhicitta, the wheel of syllables, the peaceful and wrathful maṇḍalas, empowerment, samaya and the secret instruction. It is the most commented Nyingma tantra (Rongzom, Longchenpa, Lochen Dharmaśrī, Mipham).

attribution.tradition: Taught by Samantabhadra/Vajrasattva; translated by Vimalamitra with Nyak Jñānakumāra and Ma Rinchen Chok (Nyingma histories).
attribution.scholarly: Its Indian origin was contested by 11th-13th c. critics; the Nyingma report a Sanskrit manuscript found at Samye (see dsp:authenticity-of-nyingma-tantras).

scholarly.text: translated by the late 8th-9th c. (cited in early commentaries)

attribution.tradition: Translated, according to its colophon, by the Indian abbot Dharmabodhi, Dānarakṣita and the translator Che btsan skyes from the script of Bruzha, in Bruzha.
attribution.scholarly: Its Gilgit (Bruzha) connection is noted by historians; early Anuyoga lineage via Nupchen Sangye Yeshe.

title: Kunjed Gyalpo (chos thams cad rdzogs pa chen po byang chub kyi sems kun byed rgyal po, the All-Creating King)
summary: The root tantra of the mind series in 84 chapters: bodhicitta, the 'all-creating king', speaks to Vajrasattva in the first person, teaching that everything is its own display, that there is nothing to meditate, no samaya to keep, no ground or path to traverse, and that effort is a sickness; it includes the 'six vajra lines' and other early mind-series scriptures as chapters, and restricts the teaching to fit recipients.

title: Dola Serzhun (rdo la gser zhun, Gold Refined from Ore) = Byang chub kyi sems bsgom pa (Bodhicittabhāvanā), Tōh 2591
summary: Mañjuśrīmitra's verse treatise on cultivating bodhicitta as the non-conceptual path: the awakened mind is beyond conceptual examination and verbal convention, worldly conventions of valid cognition are not needed on this yogic path, and those who seek other paths are 'like gold in ore' — worthy of compassion. One of the five early mind-series translations; preserved in the Tengyur.

title: The eighteen scriptures of the mind series (sems sde bco brgyad)

notes: The thirteen titles are given from memory and may contain errors; list for checking (REPORT.md).

title: The Seventeen Tantras of the Instruction Series (man ngag sde'i rgyud bcu bdun)
summary: The canonical tantras of the innermost secret instruction series (snying thig), taught by Samantabhadra and transmitted via Garab Dorje, Mañjuśrīmitra, Śrī Siṃha and Vimalamitra. They teach the ground, the lamps, the direct introduction, cutting through, direct crossing and its four visions, the bardos and the fruit; the Reverberation of Sound (Dra Thalgyur) is the root.

attribution.tradition: Taught by Samantabhadra; brought to Tibet by Vimalamitra and concealed; recovered by Neten Dangma Lhungyal and passed through Chetsün Senge Wangchuk and Zhangtön.

attribution.scholarly: Earliest Tibetan-attested nine-vehicle doxography; attribution not independently confirmable (moderate).

title: Cig car 'jug pa rnam par mi rtog pa'i bsgom don (The Meaning of Meditation on Non-conceptuality: the Simultaneous Entry), Tōh 3910
summary: A Madhyamaka meditation manual attributed to Vimalamitra on entering non-conceptual samādhi all at once, concluding with the aspiration that all beings gain the eye of wisdom and quickly attain omniscience. Relevant to the Samye-era question of sudden and gradual entry.

attribution.tradition: Colophon: composed by the great master Vimalamitra; translated by Dharmatāśīla and Yeshe De.

editions.name: Derge Tengyur, dbu ma, Tōh 3910 (local e-text)
editions.licence: Public domain (Derge xylograph; Esukhia/Barom digital edition, per the repository)

notes: Local: catalog:Derge-Tengyur:D3910; colophon read.

title: Samten Migdrön (bsam gtan mig sgron, the Lamp for the Eye in Contemplation)
summary: Nupchen Sangye Yeshe's treatise distinguishing four approaches to contemplation — the gradual (tsen min, of Kamalaśīla), the simultaneous (ston mun, the Chan of Moheyan), Mahāyoga and Atiyoga — ranking each above the last and so distinguishing the Great Perfection from Chan.
notes: Chapter structure not recorded; teachings given at section level (REPORT.md).

title: Tegchen Tsuljug (theg chen tshul 'jug, Entering the Way of the Great Vehicle)
summary: Rongzom Chökyi Zangpo's defence of the Great Perfection view: all appearances are like illusions, established only as appearance; perfect buddhahood is present from the beginning, and appearances are primordially pure.

title: Konchok Drel (rgyud rgyal gsang ba snying po'i 'grel pa dkon cog 'grel)
summary: Rongzom's commentary on the Guhyagarbha, a foundational statement of the 'great purity and equality' view of Mahāyoga.

title: Bashe (sba bzhed / dba' bzhed, the Testament of Ba)
summary: Early Tibetan account of the introduction of Buddhism under Trisong Detsen: the invitations of Śāntarakṣita and Padmasambhava, the building of Samye, the ordination of the first monks and the debate between the Indian and Chinese parties.

scholarly.text: core from the 9th-11th c.; several recensions

notes: Also referenced by the Samye debate (dsp:sudden-or-gradual, owned by U50).

title: The Seven Treasuries (mdzod bdun) of Longchenpa
summary: Longchenpa's seven great treatises systematizing the whole path and above all the Great Perfection: the Wish-Fulfilling, Instruction, Dharmadhātu, Philosophical Systems, Supreme Vehicle, Words and Meanings, and Natural State treasuries.

title: Yishin Dzöd (yid bzhin rin po che'i mdzod, the Wish-Fulfilling Treasury)
summary: A graded exposition of the whole path from the human birth and impermanence through the vehicles to the Great Perfection, in 22 chapters (moderate), with Longchenpa's autocommentary Padma dkar po.

title: Mengak Dzöd (man ngag rin po che'i mdzod, the Treasury of Precious Instructions)
summary: Pith instructions arranged in numbered sets (groups of six) for practitioners of every capacity.

title: Chöying Dzöd (chos dbyings rin po che'i mdzod, the Treasury of the Dharmadhātu)
summary: Vajra verses on the Great Perfection of the mind series and space series: all phenomena are the display of the expanse, ungenerated, beyond effort; in 13 chapters, with the autocommentary Lung gi gter mdzod.

title: Drubta Dzöd (grub mtha' rin po che'i mdzod, the Treasury of Philosophical Systems)
summary: A doxography from non-Buddhist systems through the Buddhist vehicles and outer tantras to the three inner tantras and Atiyoga.

title: Tegchok Dzöd (theg mchog rin po che'i mdzod, the Treasury of the Supreme Vehicle)
summary: The most extensive exposition of the instruction series and the Seventeen Tantras: ground, delusion, the lamps, trekchö, tögal, the bardos and the fruit.

title: Tsigdön Dzöd (tshig don rin po che'i mdzod, the Treasury of Words and Meanings)
summary: A condensed systematization of the instruction series in eleven vajra topics, from the ground and how delusion arises, through the body's wisdom abodes, channels and lamps, the introduction and practice, to the bardo and the fruit.

title: Nelug Dzöd (gnas lugs rin po che'i mdzod, the Treasury of the Natural State)
summary: Vajra verses with autocommentary on the four 'samayas' of the Great Perfection: non-existence (med pa), evenness (phyal ba), spontaneous presence (lhun grub) and singularity (gcig pu).

title: Lunggi Terdzö (lung gi gter mdzod, the Treasury of Scriptures)
summary: Longchenpa's autocommentary on the Chöying Dzöd, supporting each vajra verse with quotations from the mind-series and instruction-series tantras.

title: Ngalso Korsum (ngal gso skor gsum, the Trilogy of Natural Ease / Finding Rest)
summary: Longchenpa's trilogy: Finding Rest in the Nature of Mind, in Meditation and in Illusion, each with autocommentaries (the 'Chariots') and summaries; a graded path from the preliminaries to the Great Perfection.

title: Semnyi Ngalso (sems nyid ngal gso, Finding Rest in the Nature of Mind)
summary: The complete graded path in verse, from the precious human birth, impermanence and suffering through refuge, bodhicitta and the tantras to the Great Perfection; commented by Longchenpa's Shingta Chenpo (Great Chariot).

title: Samten Ngalso (bsam gtan ngal gso, Finding Rest in Meditation)
summary: On meditation in three sections: the place, the person (the practitioner's qualities) and the practice (the experiences of bliss, clarity and non-thought and their pitfalls).

title: Gyuma Ngalso (sgyu ma ngal gso, Finding Rest in Illusion)
summary: On all phenomena as illusion, taught through eight similes of illusion (dream, magic show, optical illusion, mirage, echo, city of gandharvas, reflection, emanation).

title: Shingta Chenpo (shing rta chen po, the Great Chariot)
summary: Longchenpa's autocommentary on Finding Rest in the Nature of Mind.

title: Rangdrol Korsum (rang grol skor gsum, the Trilogy of Self-Liberation)
summary: Longchenpa's trilogy on the self-liberation of mind, of reality and of equality (sems nyid, chos nyid, mnyam nyid rang grol), mind-series style instructions with practice guides.

title: Chogchu Münsel (phyogs bcu mun sel, Dispelling the Darkness of the Ten Directions)
summary: Longchenpa's commentary on the Guhyagarbha, reading the Mahāyoga tantra from the standpoint of the Great Perfection; part of his Trilogy of Dispelling Darkness (mun sel skor gsum).

title: Nyingthig Yabzhi (snying thig ya bzhi, the Four Parts of the Heart-essence)
summary: Longchenpa's compilation of the instruction-series Heart-essence: the Vima Nyingthig with his Lama Yangtig, and the Khandro Nyingthig with his Khandro Yangtig, completed by his Zabmo Yangtig.

title: Lama Yangtig (bla ma yang tig, the Innermost Heart-drop of the Guru)
summary: Longchenpa's commentarial and practical instructions on the Vima Nyingthig.

title: Khandro Yangtig (mkha' 'gro yang tig, the Innermost Heart-drop of the Ḍākinī)
summary: Longchenpa's instructions on the Khandro Nyingthig.

title: Zabmo Yangtig (zab mo yang tig, the Profound Innermost Heart-drop)
summary: Longchenpa's synthesis of the Vima and Khandro Nyingthig instructions.

title: Longchen Nyingthig (klong chen snying thig, the Heart-essence of the Great Expanse)
summary: Jigme Lingpa's mind-treasure cycle received in visions of Longchenpa: preliminaries, the guru sādhana Rigdzin Düpa, the ḍākinī practice Yumka Dechen Gyalmo, the Palchen Düpa, and Dzogchen instructions including the Yeshe Lama.

tradition.text: revealed from 1757 in three visions of Longchenpa at Samye Chimphu

title: Yeshe Lama (ye shes bla ma, the Supreme Wisdom)
summary: Jigme Lingpa's practice guide to the Longchen Nyingthig's Dzogchen: preliminaries of separating saṃsāra and nirvāṇa (ru shan), the introduction, cutting through, direct crossing, the bardo instructions and the fruit.

title: Namkhyen Lamzang (rnam mkhyen lam bzang, the Excellent Path to Omniscience: the Longchen Nyingthig preliminaries)
summary: The liturgy of the Longchen Nyingthig preliminaries: the four thoughts, refuge, bodhicitta, Vajrasattva, maṇḍala, kusāli and guru yoga with the four empowerments.

title: Rigdzin Düpa (rig 'dzin 'dus pa, the Gathering of Vidyādharas)
summary: The outer guru sādhana of the Longchen Nyingthig centred on Padmasambhava.

title: Yumka Dechen Gyalmo (yum ka bde chen rgyal mo, the Queen of Great Bliss)
summary: The inner ḍākinī sādhana of the Longchen Nyingthig centred on Yeshe Tsogyal as Queen of Great Bliss.

title: Yönten Dzöd (yon tan rin po che'i mdzod, the Treasury of Precious Qualities)
summary: Jigme Lingpa's verse summa of the whole path through the nine vehicles: the precious human birth, the sūtra path, the outer and inner tantras and the Great Perfection, with the fruit; commented by his disciples.

title: Senge Ngaro (seng ge'i nga ro, the Lion's Roar)
summary: Jigme Lingpa's instruction exposing deviations and errors in Great Perfection practice (moderate confidence on title and scope).

title: Kathang Zangling Ma (bka' thang zangs gling ma, the Copper Island biography)
summary: The earliest full treasure biography of Padmasambhava, revealed by Nyangral Nyima Özer: his lotus birth in Oḍḍiyāna, training, arrival in Tibet, the building of Samye, the taming of spirits, his teachings to the king and disciples and his departure to the land of the rākṣasas.

title: Pema Kathang (padma bka' thang, the Chronicle of Padma; Shelbrag Ma)
summary: The most famous biography of Padmasambhava, a treasure revealed by Orgyen Lingpa in 1352 at Crystal Cave (Shel brag): the Lotus-born's birth, deeds in India, the eight manifestations, the founding of Samye and the prophecies.

title: Chöjung Metok Nyingpo (chos 'byung me tog snying po sbrang rtsi'i bcud)
summary: Nyangral Nyima Özer's history of the Dharma in India and Tibet, with the early Nyingma accounts of the royal period.

title: Kagye Deshek Düpa (bka' brgyad bde gshegs 'dus pa, the Gathering of the Sugatas of the Eight Pronouncements)
summary: Nyangral Nyima Özer's treasure cycle uniting the practices of the Eight Herukas (bka' brgyad) in one maṇḍala.

title: Kagye Sangwa Yongdzog (bka' brgyad gsang ba yongs rdzogs)
summary: Guru Chöwang's treasure cycle of the Eight Herukas.

title: Lama Sangdü (bla ma gsang 'dus, the Gathering of the Guru's Secrets)
summary: Guru Chöwang's guru sādhana treasure centred on Padmasambhava.

title: Terjung Chenmo (gter 'byung chen mo, the Great History of Treasures)
summary: Guru Chöwang's account of treasure revelation — how teachings are concealed, entrusted and recovered — the earliest systematic Tibetan treatise on terma (moderate).

title: Kuntuzangpo Gongpa Zangthal (kun tu bzang po'i dgongs pa zang thal, the Unobstructed Intention of Samantabhadra)
summary: Rigdzin Gödem's Northern Treasure Dzogchen cycle in several volumes: instruction-series teachings on the ground, trekchö and tögal, and the Aspiration of Samantabhadra.

title: Kuntuzangpo Mönlam (kun tu bzang po'i smon lam stobs po che, the Powerful Aspiration of Samantabhadra)
summary: The aspiration spoken by the primordial buddha: one ground, two paths and two results — awareness and ignorance; Samantabhadra was liberated by recognizing the ground, beings wander by not recognizing it; the prayer turns each of the five poisons into its wisdom.

title: Lama Gongdü (bla ma dgongs 'dus, the Gathering of the Guru's Intentions)
summary: Sangye Lingpa's vast treasure cycle of Padmasambhava practice (revealed 1364), a principal source of Nyingma guru sādhanas.

title: Zhitro Gongpa Rangdrol (zab chos zhi khro dgongs pa rang grol, the Profound Dharma of Self-Liberation through the Intention of the Peaceful and Wrathful Ones)
summary: Karma Lingpa's treasure cycle of the hundred peaceful and wrathful deities, including the instructions on the six bardos, the signs of death, the purification of the dead and the 'Great Liberation through Hearing'.

title: Bardo Thödol Chenmo (bar do thos grol chen mo, the Great Liberation through Hearing in the Intermediate States)
summary: The part of Karma Lingpa's cycle read aloud to the dying and dead: it introduces the clear light at the moment of death, the peaceful and wrathful deities of the bardo of dharmatā day by day as one's own projections, and the ways to close the womb door or choose a birth in the bardo of becoming.
alt_titles: The Tibetan Book of the Dead

tradition.text: concealed by Padmasambhava; revealed by Karma Lingpa on Mount Gampodar

title: Bardo Tsigkyi (bar do'i rtsa tshig, the Root Verses of the Six Bardos)
summary: The verses of the six intermediate states (life, dream, meditation, dying, dharmatā, becoming), each exhorting the practitioner to recognize and use that bardo.

title: Chitak Tsenma Rangdrol ('chi ltas mtshan ma rang grol, Self-Liberation of the Signs of Death)
summary: Karma Lingpa's text on the outer, inner and secret signs of approaching death and the rites to avert premature death.

title: Kunzang Gongdü (kun bzang dgongs 'dus, the Gathering of Samantabhadra's Intentions)
summary: Pema Lingpa's principal treasure cycle, covering Dzogchen and sādhanas; basis of the Bhutanese Peling tradition.

title: Tsigdün Söldeb (tshig bdun gsol 'debs, the Seven-Line Prayer to Padmasambhava)
summary: The best-known prayer to Guru Rinpoche, invoking the Lotus-born of the north-west border of Oḍḍiyāna, found in many treasure cycles and recited daily across the Nyingma.
notes: Its treasure attributions are several; not tied here to one revealer.

title: Le'u Dünma (gsol 'debs le'u bdun ma, the Prayer in Seven Chapters)
summary: A treasure prayer to Padmasambhava in seven chapters, each spoken by the Guru to a disciple (Yeshe Tsogyal, the king, Namkhai Nyingpo...), including the prayer that spontaneously fulfils wishes (Sampa Lhundrupma).

title: Kunzang Lamai Shelung (kun bzang bla ma'i zhal lung, the Words of My Perfect Teacher)
summary: Patrul Rinpoche's oral-style guide to the Longchen Nyingthig preliminaries as taught by Jigme Gyalwai Nyugu: Part One the common outer preliminaries (freedoms and advantages, impermanence, the defects of saṃsāra, karma, the benefits of liberation, following a teacher); Part Two the uncommon inner preliminaries (refuge, bodhicitta, Vajrasattva, maṇḍala, kusāli, guru yoga); Part Three the transference of consciousness (phowa) as an auxiliary.

structure.description: 3 parts: 6 outer chapters, 6 inner chapters, phowa

title: Khepa Shri Gyalpoi Khyechö (mkhas pa shri rgyal po'i khyad chos, the Special Teaching of the Wise and Glorious King)
summary: Patrul Rinpoche's verses with autocommentary on Garab Dorje's three statements.

title: Ngeshe Drönme (nges shes rin po che'i sgron me, the Beacon of Certainty)
summary: Mipham's verse answers to seven questions on the view — whether the ultimate is an affirming or non-affirming negation, whether śrāvakas realize both selflessnesses, whether meditation involves apprehension, analytical versus resting meditation, which of the two truths is primary, how one object appears differently to different beings, and whether Madhyamaka has a thesis — reconciling Madhyamaka with the Great Perfection.

title: Norbu Ketaka (nor bu ke ta ka), Mipham's commentary on Bodhicaryāvatāra ch. 9
summary: Mipham's commentary on the wisdom chapter, which set off exchanges with Gelug scholars on Prāsaṅgika (the object of negation, whether the ultimate is beyond the four extremes).

title: Ösel Nyingpo (gsang snying spyi don 'od gsal snying po, the Essence of Clear Light)
summary: Mipham's general exposition of the Guhyagarbha: the view of great purity and equality, the 'superior two truths', and the path of Mahāyoga.

title: Khejug (mkhas pa'i tshul la 'jug pa'i sgo, the Gateway to Knowledge)
summary: Mipham's manual of the ten topics of scholarship (aggregates, elements, sense bases, dependent origination, correct and incorrect, faculties, times, truths, vehicles, compounded and uncompounded) and of the four reliances and valid cognition.

title: The Nyingma History of Dudjom Rinpoche (bstan pa'i rnam gzhag and chos 'byung)
summary: Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje's two works: the Fundamentals (the nine vehicles and their doctrines) and the History of the Nyingma (the kama and terma lineages, biographies of tertöns).

title: Nangjang (snang sbyang, Refining Apparent Phenomena)
summary: Dudjom Lingpa's visionary Dzogchen treatise in dialogue form on the ground, delusion, and the view.

title: Magom Sangye (ma bsgom sangs rgyas, Buddhahood Without Meditation)
summary: Dudjom Lingpa's Dzogchen instruction on revealing one's own face of the natural Great Perfection 'without meditation'.

title: Tukdrub Barche Künsel (thugs sgrub bar chad kun sel, the Heart Practice Dispelling All Obstacles)
summary: The guru sādhana cycle of Padmasambhava revealed by Chokgyur Lingpa with Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

title: Rinchen Terdzö (rin chen gter mdzod, the Treasury of Precious Treasures)
summary: Jamgön Kongtrul's collection of the principal treasure cycles of all revealers, with empowerment rites and the biographies of the hundred tertöns; enlarged after him.

title: Tertön Gyatsa (gter ston brgya rtsa, the Hundred Tertöns)
summary: Jamgön Kongtrul's biographies of the treasure revealers, with an explanation of the treasure tradition.

title: Zermig (gzer mig, the Piercing Eye)
summary: One of the three biographies of Tönpa Shenrab: his descent from the heavens, birth in Ölmo Lungring, his deeds, the pursuit of the demon Khyapa Lagring who stole his horses into Tibet, and his teaching.
notes: Optional (Bön). Not local; from general knowledge.

scholarly.text: treasure text of c. the 11th c.

title: Zijid (gzi brjid, the Glorious)
summary: The longest biography of Tönpa Shenrab (twelve volumes), transmitted by Loden Nyingpo; its exposition of the nine ways of Bön is the classical source for them.
notes: Optional (Bön). Not local; from general knowledge.

tradition.text: an oral/mind transmission received by Loden Nyingpo

title: Dodü (mdo 'dus, the Condensed Sūtra)
summary: The shortest of the three biographies of Tönpa Shenrab.
notes: Optional (Bön). Not local; from general knowledge.

title: Zhang Zhung Nyengyü (zhang zhung snyan rgyud, the Oral Transmission of Zhang Zhung)
summary: Bön's principal Dzogchen corpus: Tapihritsa's instructions to Gyerpung Nangzher Löpo arranged in four cycles — the outer (general view), inner (pith instructions), secret (seeing awareness nakedly) and innermost secret (decisive knowledge of the natural state) — with the experiential transmission and biographies of the lineage.
notes: Optional (Bön). Not local; from general knowledge.

tradition.text: orally transmitted from the 8th c. without concealment

title: A-tri (a khrid, the Instruction on the Primordial A)
summary: The Bön Dzogchen meditation system based on fixation on the white letter A, founded by Meu Gongdzö Ritrö Chenpo and later arranged in fifteen sessions (moderate).
notes: Optional (Bön). Not local; from general knowledge.

title: Dzogchen Yangtse Longchen (rdzogs chen yang rtse klong chen, the Great Expanse of the Highest Peak)
summary: The treasure-based 'Dzogchen' cycle of Bön, the third of Bön's three Dzogchen systems (A-tri, Dzogchen, Nyengyü).
notes: Optional (Bön). Not local; from general knowledge.

title: Gyalwa Chaktri (rgyal ba phyag khrid, the Manual of the Victorious Ones)
summary: Dru Gyalwa Yungdrung's practice manual for the Zhang Zhung Nyengyü, from preliminaries to the practices of the natural state (low-moderate).
notes: Optional (Bön). Not local; from general knowledge.

title: Ma Gyü (ma rgyud sangs rgyas rgyud gsum, the Mother Tantra)
summary: The principal Bön mother tantra, source of Bön practices of channels and winds, dream and sleep yoga and bardo instruction (low).
notes: Optional (Bön). Not local; from general knowledge.

title: Sipai Dzöpuk (srid pa'i mdzod phug, the Treasury of Existence)
summary: The Bön cosmological and abhidharma root text, with commentary attributed to Drenpa Namkha (low).
notes: Optional (Bön). Not local; from general knowledge.

title: The Bön Kangyur (bon gyi bka' 'gyur)
summary: The canon of the words of Tönpa Shenrab, arranged in sūtra (mdo), perfection of wisdom ('bum), tantra (rgyud) and knowledge (mdzod) sections.
notes: Optional (Bön). Not local; from general knowledge.

title: The Bön Tengyur (bon gyi brten 'gyur / bka' brten)
summary: The collection of commentaries and treatises of the Bön canon.
notes: Optional (Bön). Not local; from general knowledge.

title: Legshe Rinpoche Dzöd (legs bshad rin po che'i mdzod, the Treasury of Good Sayings)
summary: Shardza Tashi Gyaltsen's history of Bön: its origins in Tagzig and Zhang Zhung, the persecutions, the treasures and the lineages.
notes: Optional (Bön). Not local; from general knowledge.

title: Kusum Rangshar (sku gsum rang shar, the Self-Arising Three Bodies)
summary: Shardza Tashi Gyaltsen's Dzogchen instruction manual (low confidence on title and scope).
notes: Optional (Bön). Not local; from general knowledge.
